stagedNotShipped.wave3 knight_*_8f sheets: the previous dwarf set, superseded wholesale by this one; kept in staging/players/knight/ as the record of what the character looked like before

stagedNotShipped.barbarian_armed_walking: the other take on the axe walk; see `walk` above for why this one lost
stagedNotShipped.barbarian_walking / _running / _punch /: the unarmed loadout's locomotion and melee. Shipping them beside the axe would pop the weapon out of the character's hands on every other swing
stagedNotShipped.damage/death/recover: NO SOURCE ART EXISTS in either loadout -- all three fall back through EntityAnimationBinder. GrayscaleDeath still greys the corpse, so death reads, but the pose does not sell it
stagedNotShipped.wave3 barbarian_axe_* sheets: the previous barbarian set, superseded wholesale by this one; kept in staging/players/barbarian/ as the record of what the character looked like before

stagedNotShipped.wave3 elf_* sheets: the previous elven set, superseded wholesale by this one; kept in staging/players/elf/ as the record of what the character looked like before
stagedNotShipped.elf_archer_idle / _walking / _running: the archer loadout's LOCOMOTION. EntityAnimationBinder builds variant lists for exactly two states -- Attack and Cast -- and PlayerController.NextVariant only rotates one per action, so an idle or walk variant has no selector and would never render a frame. Shipping them needs a loadout system, not an import
stagedNotShipped.elf_bard_idle / _walking / _walking_2 /: the bard loadout's locomotion; same reason as the archer's

stagedNotShipped.vampire_idle_2: the second take on the idle. Both are clean; this one holds its arms closer and reads as the same pose six times, where the shipped sheet moves a hand to the hair
stagedNotShipped.vampire_running_3: the second take on the run, drawn 4x2. vampire_running is one row of eight with a wider stride and more even cell margins, so it wins the `chase` slot
stagedNotShipped.vampire_kick_2: the second take on the kick; the shipped one has ten frames against this one's eight and a longer wind-up
stagedNotShipped.vampire_running_attack_2: the second take on the running strike
stagedNotShipped.vampire_hit_2: the second take on the hit reaction
stagedNotShipped.vampire_knockdown_recovery_2: the second take on the rise. The shipped one opens on the blow that puts her down, so the state reads from standing to standing

stagedNotShipped.mague_staff_unequip: a purpose-drawn SHEATHE, and there is no selector for it. PlayerLoadoutController stows by playing the equip variant REVERSED -- one sheet, one motion, read either way -- and a variant is chosen by spell key, so both directions of weapon_toggle resolve to the same one. Shipping this would need the controller to name a second variant on the stow, which is a runtime change rather than an art import
stagedNotShipped.an unarmed idle: DOES NOT EXIST in the wave. The base idle therefore holds the staff, which is visible for as long as the character stands still with the `armed` loadout off. Six frames of a wizard standing still, empty-handed, closes it
stagedNotShipped.legacy mague_idle / _walking / _casting: the previous 8-direction 128px strips, superseded wholesale by this wave
